title: Attribute-driven usage slices and observer-role constraints for analytics endpoints
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Several console usage endpoints return wide, tenant-spanning usage rows that leak attribute-level details (team, feature_flag, dataset) to consumers with broad read access. We need a server-side enforcement layer that produces narrow, attribute-driven "slices" of usage data for roles that should only observe bounded telemetry (for auditors, security-read roles, and external partners). This must work for both ad-hoc queries (series endpoints, ad-hoc SQL exports) and precomputed views (materialized rollups) and must support temporal redaction windows used by compliance (e.g., GDPR purge windows).

Goals: 
- Implement attribute-driven query-slicing that rewrites or gates analytics queries based on caller entitlements and configured visibility rules.
- Support an "observer" role which can see aggregated metrics but not sensitive attribute values; for example, map team IDs to "team:masked" unless explicit entitlement exists.
- Apply temporal redaction where time windows older than a retention cutoff are available only as lower-resolution aggregates.
- Keep latency impact within SLOs for critical routes (95th percentile query latency increase <= 15%).
- Provide clear migration and rollback path behind a feature flag and canary by tenant.

Scope: console backend usage endpoints (GET /v1/usage/series, /v1/usage/table, /v1/usage/exports), analytics gateway layer, entitlement cache, and materialized view annotation. Not in scope: UI changes, long-term storage format changes (follow-up work).

Non-goals: full attribute-level encryption, per-row cryptographic access control (future work).
acceptance_criteria: Requests from observer-role accounts cannot return raw attribute identifiers (team_id, dataset_id) unless entitlement present.
Query planner rewrites do not change numerical aggregates; only masking and rollup resolution differ.
Canary rollout by tenant flag with telemetry to track access-denied-rate, query-latency, and mismatch-rate against current baseline.
Automated integration tests that validate mask/no-mask across 5 example tenants and temporal redaction behavior.
Security review sign-off and KMS audit of redaction keys/configs completed.
Migration script to backfill materialized view annotations and entitlement mappings executed with <1h downtime for metadata service.
Feature disabled by default; must be enabled per-tenant via console flag and API.
Documentation for operations and runbooks added to Confluence and linked in ticket.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Centralized enforcement in the analytics gateway vs. DB-level policy: chose gateway-level query rewriting because it allows consistent behavior across exporters and materialized views and avoids DB schema changes onboarding complexity.
Masking vs. filtering: prefer masking attribute values to empty results for observer roles to avoid breaking dashboards that expect cardinality; masking policy keeps rollups stable.

Materialized view annotation approach: add visibility metadata to view manifests instead of creating new views per role to reduce storage churn; requires a view-metadata join at query time which is acceptable with caching.

Temporal redaction at resolution boundaries: implement coarse-graining (hour->day->month) rather than deleting rows to preserve analytics continuity for long windows while satisfying compliance retention.

Entitlement cache staleness: we accept eventual consistency (max 30s) for entitlement changes to avoid synchronous auth lookups in hot paths; documented trade-off and compensating controls for emergency revocations.
implementation_plan: Step 1: Schema + manifest - add 'visibility' annotations to existing materialized view manifest store (no new tables).
Step 2: Entitlement shape - stabilize attribute->entitlement mappings and publish schema; implement fast TTLed Redis cache in analytics gateway.
Step 3: Query rewrite layer - implement AST-based rewrite for our SQL subset used in usage endpoints to transform SELECT clauses and WHEREs according to masks and redaction rules.
Step 4: Runtime enforcement - add per-tenant feature flag and tenant-canary support in gateway; integrate with token introspection to map caller->roles.
Step 5: Tests and perf - add unit and integration tests; run perf harness against representative load and tune cache/plan heuristics.
Step 6: Canary rollout - enable for 5 internal tenants, monitor metrics and error budgets, then widen to customer canary group before global enablement.
Step 7: Documentation + runbooks - write operations guide for emergency disable and entitlement backfill procedures.
rollout_and_migration: Canary cohort: internal-test-1..5 tenants, then 10 pilot customers identified with account managers.
Backfill: one-time job to annotate existing materialized views with visibility rules; job runs in schema-only mode and is idempotent.
Rollback: flip feature flag off per tenant; cache TTL expiration ensures eventual return to prior state.
Monitoring: dashboards console.usage.access_denied_rate, console.usage.query_latency_pct95, console.usage.mask_mismatch_rate, and alert on >2x increase in timeouts.
Data migration window: plan for low-traffic maintenance window for the backfill (target < 1 hour).
test_plan: Unit: AST rewrite unit tests for 120 query templates covering group-bys, top-n, and join patterns.
Integration: end-to-end tests against staging materialized views with 5 tenant roles exercising masked vs unmasked queries.
Perf: 95th percentile latency regression test (target <= +15% over baseline) using existing perf harness workload 'usage-heavy-2026'.
Security: threat model review and red-team attempt to bypass masking via crafted queries.
E2E: smoke via UI dashboards for canary tenants to confirm no broken charts.
observability_and_success_metrics: Access-denied-rate: expected increase during canary as masks apply; target < 5% of queries flagged.
Mask-mismatch-rate: queries where masking changes cardinality unexpectedly; target < 0.5%.
False-negative leakage tests: zero allowed leaks in automated test set.
Operator alerts for entitlement-sync fails or cache hit-rate < 90%.
Canary adoption metric: % of pilot tenants flipped successfully and stable for 7 days.
security_and_compliance_notes: This feature interacts with retention policies; coordinate with Legal for temporal redaction windows for EU accounts.
KMS usage for any redaction keys/configuration; audit trail must be enabled for changes to visibility manifests.
Security review required before first customer canary; include threat model and wire-level logging review.
Emergency revocation path must invalidate cache and block responses until entitlement service confirms.
open_risks: Complex queries with non-standard joins may defeat AST rewrite heuristics and cause either incorrect masking or query failures.
Cache staleness could permit short windows where revoked entitlements still see data (30s window).
Materialized view annotation approach may not cover externally managed exports; will require export adapter in follow-up.
